title: Twenty Units
sceneText:
When today’s load is in, Gregor counts it over in the yard. He counts slowly, and when he has finished he counts it again.

“Twenty,” he says.

You say the allowance is twenty-five.

“Mm.”

He puts the marking pencil back in his pocket and looks at the stack.

“Twenty-five is what the decree says. The decree is written for the whole north district.”

He pauses.

“Oak on this slope takes sixty years to come to a size worth cutting. Cut twenty-five this year and next year you cut further north. What is further north is a steep face. Cut that and the soil will not hold.”

Then he goes to see to the horses.

He did not say not to cut it. He only said the thing once.

choices.text: Take the remaining five units as planned

effects.logEntry: You cut the season’s allowance out to the full.

choices.resultText:
You took the last five units.

Nothing was broken. The books are clean: twenty-five units, not one over.

When the last load came in Gregor came to take the cart. He unloaded as usual and led the horses off as usual and said nothing.

Those five units sat in the yard three days before they were carried away.

choices.text: Stop here. Leave the rest of the allowance unused

effects.logEntry: You stopped the season’s felling at twenty units.

choices.resultText:
You say that is far enough.

Gregor is untying a rein, and his hands stop for half a second.

“Mm.”

He goes on untying the rein.

That evening when you go to the stable he is standing in the doorway. He does not usually stand in the doorway.

“That ground to the north,” he says. “My father’s generation cut it once. Half the slope came down that winter.”

“Was it planted back?”

“It was,” he says. “It has come up this thick now.”

He shows you with his hand. Less than a span.

“Sixty years.”
